relevance_note: Case series of three children with PAMI syndrome, each described individually: "all 3 patients had PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K) spontaneous heterozygous mutations".
method_note: Read the whole paper; values written by hand into a Python builder script, which looked up every span in the paper (the paper uses thin spaces, e.g. in "c.748G > A" and "× 10^9/L"; spans keep them). Table 1 and Table 2 have patients as columns (headers "Patient 1/2/3" and "patient1/2/3"); spans quote the row from its label through that patient's cell. Scope: Patients 1-3 (all with PSTPIP1 c.748G>A p.E250K) plus the father and mother of each, whose Sanger maps are shown in Figs. 3, 4 and 7 (tested relatives; no features or variant rows for them). Table symbols: Table 1 '–' and Table 2 '–' and 'N' are not defined in the paper, so those cells are recorded as not reported (e.g. acne '–' for all three, fever '–' for Patient 2, PG '–' for Patient 3); only the word 'Normal' (C3, Patients 1-2) was used as an exclusion (low C3). Table 2 numeric values that the text does not call abnormal were not turned into features. Inheritance recorded as de novo from "identified by Sanger in three family lines ... spontaneous mutations in probands", the parental Sanger maps in the figure legends, and "All three children had spontaneous mutations, which were wild-type" (read as parents wild-type; the sentence is garbled). Zygosity from the abstract's named group statement "all 3 patients ... heterozygous". In-silico predictions (SIFT, PolyPhen_2, REVEL) are not functional evidence or an authors' classification, so those fields are not reported. Ages not recorded: the case sections give ages at past events ("Three years ago, an 8-year-old", "Eight years ago, a 10-year-old", "Ten years ago, a 13-year-old"), not stated as onset, diagnosis or last evaluation, and the abstract's ages (6 y 5 m, 8 y 7 m, 13 y 3 m) are not attributed to individual patients. 'Bone marrow aspiration was normal' and 'normal humoral immunity' (Patient 3) are whole investigations and were recorded as written ('abnormal bone marrow aspiration', 'abnormal humoral immunity' excluded). Contradictions in the paper: (1) sex - Patient 1 is 'female'/'she' in the case section but 'His rash' in the Discussion; Patient 3 is 'male' but 'her condition did not improve'; sex taken from the case sections. (2) Patient 1 hepatosplenomegaly appears only in the Discussion ('His rash, trilineage hypoplasia, and hepatosplenomegaly improved'); the case section mentions only the spleen. Recorded as observed with that span, but it may be a mix-up with another patient. (3) Patient 1 ESR: the abstract says all three had elevated ESR, Table 2 gives 'N' for Patient 1 and the Discussion says 'patients 2 and 3 had faster AESR'; the elevated-ESR row for Patient 1 comes from the abstract group statement, and the checklist uses CRP. (4) Patient 3: text gives WBC 7.83 and PLT 883 x10^9/L while Table 2 gives 1.75 and 45; anemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia left not reported for Patient 3 because no value is called abnormal. (5) Patient 1 treatment duration: abstract '8 months' vs 'followed up for two years'. Trilineage hypoplasia is recorded as its own feature and not used to set anemia/neutropenia/thrombocytopenia on the checklist. Patient 2 anemia on the checklist rests on 'reduced RBC'; her hip abscess (joint) is not counted as a skin or soft-tissue abscess; faecal calprotectin 72.4 is not labelled elevated and is faecal, so hypercalprotectinemia is not reported. Patient 1 Ludwig's angina ('considered to have') is recorded as a feature but not as a soft-tissue abscess.

study_type.span: This study retrospectively analysed the clinical and genetic data of three children with PAMI syndrome in our hospital between April 2018 and January 2020.

n_patients_reported.span: Genetic testing showed that all 3 patients had PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K) spontaneous heterozygous mutations

cohort_size_as_stated.span: We retrospectively analysed clinical data and genetic testing results of three children with PAMI syndrome

individual_label_in_paper.span: ### Patient 1

is_proband.span: all of which were identified as spontaneous mutations in probands

treatment_summary.value: Intravenous human immunoglobulin 2 g/kg (ineffective); oral methylprednisolone (1 mg/kg/d) and cyclosporine (4 mg/kg/d), later reduced to 3 mg/d and 75 mg/d; mandibular swelling disappeared, blood cell count and CRP returned to normal, splenomegaly recovered
span: Intravenous human immunoglobulin therapy 2 g/kg was ineffective.
Oral Methylprednisolone (1 mg/kg/d) and cyclosporine (4 mg/kg/d) were administered, and the left mandibular swelling gradually disappeared
Methylprednisolone and cyclosporine was reduced to 3 mg/d and 75 mg/d, respectively.
Her blood cell count and CRP levels returned to normal. Her splenomegaly recovered.
Patient 1 was treated with a combination of methylprednisolone and cyclosporine for 8 months.

disease_label_as_stated.span: Therefore, she was diagnosed with PAMI syndrome.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing: whole-exome testing found PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K), leading to the diagnosis
span: The whole-exome gene testing was completed and suggested a spontaneous PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K)
Therefore, she was diagnosed with PAMI syndrome.

individual_label_in_paper.span: ### Patient 2

is_proband.span: all of which were identified as spontaneous mutations in probands

treatment_summary.value: Symptomatic blood transfusion; antibiotics, component blood transfusion and IVIG for hip; infliximab 5 mg/kg twice (allergic reaction, discontinued); oral colchicine 0.125 mg for 1 month (ineffective); etanercept 0.8 mg/kg weekly plus oral methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg daily; for PG, local debridement, antibiotics and methylprednisolone increased to 6 mg/d
span: Symptomatic blood transfusion treatment was given.
The joint symptoms improved following the treatment of antibiotics, component blood transfusion, and intravenous human immunoglobulin.
After administration of infliximab 5 mg/kg twice, the patient developed an allergic reaction. So we discontinued inflicimab, and started oral colchicine 0.125 mg for 1 month, which was ineffective.
Therefore, we changed to subcutaneous injection of etanercept (0.8 mg/kg) once a week and methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg orally once a day.
we did local debridement and gave her antibiotic. In addition, we increased methylprednisolone to 6 mg/d.

disease_label_as_stated.span: hence, the diagnosis of PAMI syndrome was made.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing: whole-exome testing found PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K), leading to the diagnosis
clinical_diagnosis_basis.span: Whole-exome genetic testing suggested a spontaneous PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K) mutation (see Fig. 4 for gene mutation profile), hence, the diagnosis of PAMI syndrome was made.

individual_label_in_paper.span: ### Patient 3

is_proband.span: all of which were identified as spontaneous mutations in probands

treatment_summary.value: Splenectomy; aniracetam 2.5 mg qd and tadalafil 10 mg qd for pulmonary hypertension with cardiotonic diuresis (no considerable improvement); oral methylprednisolone (initially 20 mg once a day, tapered), oral methotrexate 10 mg, intravenous infliximab 6 mg/kg, 4 times
span: a 13-year-old male patient underwent splenectomy for trilineage hypoplasia
Aniracetam 2.5 mg qd and tadalafil 10 mg qd were prescribed as targeted therapy for pulmonary hypertension and symptomatic cardiotonic diuresis. However, her condition did not improve considerably.

The patient was prescribed oral methylprednisolone 0.5 mg/kg every two weeks, followed by oral methotrexate 10 mg after four weeks, and intravenous infliximab 6 mg/kg after eight weeks, totally 4 times.
The initial treatment of methylprednisolone was 20 mg once a day. Then the dose was reduced by 4 mg per month until 8 mg QD, following by reduction of 2 mg per month.

disease_label_as_stated.span: Therefore, the diagnosis of PAMI syndrome was established.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing: whole-exome testing found PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K), leading to the diagnosis
span: Whole-exome genetic testing was performed, and the results suggested a spontaneous PSTPIP1 c.748G > A (p.E250K)
Therefore, the diagnosis of PAMI syndrome was established.
